topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular differentiation, genetic alterations, and modeling of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes disrupt normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, and how these processes are modeled experimentally.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors, invasion, progression, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: They define the biological, histological, and diagnostic distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, including invasion pathways, stepwise progression, and naming conventions.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the physical, metabolic, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Comparative cancer incidence across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze the incidence and tissue distribution of tumors across human populations and other multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the principles, histological basis, and clinical effectiveness of screening and early detection across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical session reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture and provides administrative reminders for upcoming practical sessions and lectures.
